summary.headline: DLF Q2 FY27 booked INR 3,800 crore sales and reported INR 2,298 crore revenue, aided by a one-time INR 738 crore fair-value gain in other income.
summary.overview: DLF reported new sales bookings of about INR 3,800 crore and collections of INR 2,780 crore, with operating cash flow of about INR 1,858 crore and net cash of about INR 15,100 crore after roughly INR 1,980 crore of dividend payout. Consolidated revenue of INR 2,298 crore included a one-time INR 738 crore valuation gain on a JV investment booked as other income, with EBITDA of INR 1,060 crore and net profit above INR 1,300 crore. Rental portfolio reached 50 million sq ft at 96% occupancy by area and 97% by value. Management said accounting revenue remains back-ended under completed-contract accounting until the pre-Arbour projects complete in FY28. Management flagged likely Q3 construction outflow slowdown from labour migration and Delhi GRAP restrictions.

financial_highlights.change: includes one-time INR 738 crore gain booked as other income

segments.name: Development (DLF)
segments.commentary: Aureva luxury retirement housing sold out; Dahlias super-luxury sales at about 276 units sold so far with prices up about 10% this quarter. Gross margin potential of development business about INR 40,000 crore, cash generation potential over INR 42,500 crore.

segments.name: Rental (DLF portfolio)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 96% occupancy by area and 97% by value; quarterly rental about INR 120 crore, with full-potential exit run-rate of INR 175-180 crore per quarter (about INR 750 crore annualised), excluding Atrium.

segments.name: DCCDL (commercial annuity)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,014 crore, EBITDA INR 1,537 crore, net profit over INR 750 crore (+17% YoY). Exit rental guidance about INR 6,800 crore.

guidance_outlook: Accounting revenue inflection expected in FY27-28 as launched projects (about INR 75,000 crore launched so far) complete and are recognised under completed-contract method, continuing over next two to five years.
Arbour commissioning targeted FY27-28, followed by a series of project completions; completion timelines seen as broadly within a quarter of plan.
Experience Centre for Dahlias targeted by December; Mumbai launch in Q3 and Gurugram launch plus a new luxury-plus project in Phase 4 (Hamilton, unnamed) targeted in Q4.
Forward other expenses to be in line with average of last two quarters; other income expected at about INR 150-200 crore per quarter excluding one-offs.
DLF dividend guidance remains annual; DCCDL to provide more predictable dividend flow to DLF.

DCCDL completions: Goa Promenade around Christmas/New Year, Downtown Gurugram Block 7 and Chennai Blocks 4-5 (3.6 mn sq ft) in FY28/calendar 2027; Mall of India Gurugram in FY30; most DCCDL blocks operational FY29-FY30.
capex_capacity: Rental portfolio 50 mn sq ft; Atrium fully rent-generating this year; Summit Plaza and Midtown Plaza commissioned this quarter.
Chennai Blocks 1-3 operational; Chennai Blocks 4-5 (3.6 mn sq ft) to become operational by calendar 2027.
Downtown Gurugram Blocks 5-8 and Mall of India Gurugram: completion targeted end-FY28 to FY29, most blocks operational FY29-FY30.

Land: acquired remaining 7.06-acre encumbered parcel from IREO bonds transaction and a fresh 7.48-acre contiguous parcel in Sector 61, creating a 36-acre contiguous land parcel; land deal expected to conclude by Q4.
Construction outflows expected to be slightly weaker in Q2-Q3 due to labour migration for Chhath and GRAP restrictions (30-40 days typical in Gurgaon).
demand_pricing: Dahlias: price up about 10% this quarter with algorithmic increase on each sale; North units at about INR 120-125 crore for 10,000 sq ft and a penthouse at INR 271 crore; North-South price gap about INR 20-25 crore.
Dahlias South sale reached about INR 100 crore per apartment, described as a new landmark.
Average realisation on saleable area well above INR 1,00,000 per sq ft this quarter.
Super-luxury gross sales about INR 19 hundred crore this quarter (including The Camellias, as stated).
Aureva booking amount INR 50 lakh; about INR 1,900 crore of INR 1,985 crore potential reported in the quarter, with about six units spilling over into October on NRI payment confirmations.
Q1 described as relatively quiet for pre-sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Aureva sales extend into October and are Dahlias price hikes already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales closed before 30 September; only money-received and KYC-complete units are booked, so about INR 1,900 crore of INR 1,985 crore was booked in Q2 and the rest was recorded in October. Dahlias prices already rose about 10% this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exit rental run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-potential quarterly rent of about INR 175-180 crore (about INR 750 crore annualised) for DLF portfolio excluding Atrium; DCCDL exit rental about INR 6,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will construction outflows slow and will completion timelines hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a slight blip in Q2-Q3 construction outflows due to labour migration and GRAP; completion timelines seen as broadly within a quarter, with no major challenges foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: Could dividends move to quarterly or half-yearly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; DLF dividend remains annual, though DCCDL dividend flow to DLF is being made more predictable.

qa_highlights.question: Why are accounting revenues below expectations and what drives other expenses and other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Completed-contract accounting defers recognition to OC; inflection in FY27-28. Cyber City (about INR 2,000 crore quarterly revenue) and Atrium Place (INR 150-175 crore) are not consolidated despite 67% control due to minority AVM rights. Other expenses are overheads in line with prior average; other income guidance INR 150-200 crore per quarter excluding one-offs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hamilton project and when will it launch?
qa_highlights.answer: Unnamed luxury-plus project in DLF Phase 4 near the same vicinity, targeted for launch in Q4.

risks_watch: Accounting revenue remains depressed until pre-Arbour projects complete; FY27-28 inflection is key.
Construction outflow slowdown in Q2-Q3 from labour migration and Delhi GRAP; 30-40 GRAP days typical in Gurgaon.
One-time INR 738 crore fair-value gain inflates Q2 profit; underlying profit much lower.
Launch timing dependent on approvals (Mumbai, Gurgaon); Experience Centre timing could slip due to GRAP.
Cyber City and Atrium Place excluded from consolidated revenue despite 67% stake, reducing reported revenue visibility.
Delhi Master Plan impact on Midtown and Chanakyapuri still early-stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and rental momentum, but cautious and somewhat defensive on accounting revenue, construction outflows and launch timing. Management repeatedly framed the weak revenue as a temporary completed-contract phase and flagged GRAP risk without quantifying it.
key_quotes: Dahlias has been seeing a price increase. In fact, it's already gone up by almost about 10% even this time.
So, we report what is recorded in our financial system.
Fundamentally, the three key drivers of our business, which is strong pre-sales of the identified products.
